newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TVB deal shows Shaw Brothers' confidence.
newsitem.headline: TVB deal shows Shaw Brothers' confidence.

text.p: Shaw Brothers (Hong Kong) Ltd's recent purchase of another 10 percent in Television Broadcasts Ltd (TVB) from Pearson Plc shows its confidence in the future of the television station, analysts said on Monday.

"It (the deal) will have very little impact on the fundamentals of the company but I think it does imply the Shaw family is very confident about TVB's future and they see profit picking up," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Mark Siford said.
Shaw Brothers and its associate the Shaw Foundation Hong Kong Ltd agreed to buy 21 million TVB shares each, accounting for about 10 percent of TVB, from Pearson at HK$33.25 per share.
After the deal Shaw Brothers and its associates would hold about 34.33 percent of Hong Kong's leading broadcaster.

Siford said Pearson had not brought much business to TVB since it bought the 10 percent stake two years ago from Shaw Brothers. "Pearson was a passive investor anyway," added Vickers Ballas analyst Vincent Kwan.
The British media and publishing conglomerate bought the 10 percent stake in TVB to get more exposure to the Asian media market but had changed its focus since then, analysts said.
They said it was sensible for Pearson to get out now with a small profit.
But Siford said Pearson's sale came a bit too early. "Even if they are making a small profit now, I think they should hold on because I think that TVB is just going into an upturn now."
Pearson sold the stake for 111.1 million pounds after acquiring it two years ago at 106.2 million pounds. It has received dividends of 3.5 million pounds on its shares.
Morgan Grenfell forecast a rise of about six percent in TVB's 1996 net profit to HK$516 million and a rise of about 31 percent in 1997 to HK$678 million.

Vickers sees TVB's net profit rising about nine percent to HK$532 million in 1996 and estimates net profit of HK$604 million in 1997. TVB shares closed unchanged on Monday at HK$34. Only 260,000 shares worth HK$8.84 million were traded.
"My target is HK$40 for 12 months," Siford said. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
